trigger_input.complaint: Every evening it crawls, fine during the day

signals.value: 1.19 kbps last reading, down from 4.82 kbps first reading and 5.72 kbps 7-day mean
signals.threshold: Current speed is below the observed 7-day mean; no calibrated speed band is provided

detection.summary: The customer reports evening slowdown and the observed speed trend is materially below its recent mean, while optical power, sessions, router health, and OLT status remain within their calibrated or healthy bands.

diagnosis.root_cause: The evening-only slowdown and large speed decline are most consistent with shared PON bandwidth congestion. The optical link is stable and normal, authentication and VLAN provisioning are correct, sessions are normal, and the OLT and PON remain responsive. Direct utilization counters were not provided, so the congestion diagnosis is probable rather than conclusive.
evidence: Speed declined from 4.82 kbps at the start of the 168-hour series to 1.19 kbps at the latest reading, with a 7-day mean of 5.72 kbps.
The customer specifically reports that performance degrades every evening and is fine during the day, which is consistent with time-dependent shared capacity contention.
Current RX power is -21.27 dBm and TX power is 2.37 dBm, both within calibrated normal ranges.
RX variation over the week was only 0.71 dBm with a change of -0.13 dBm; distance was constant at 167 m, so there is no evidence of fibre degradation or a path change.
TX bias current remained healthy and essentially flat at 11.19 mA mean with a change of 0.04 mA, providing no indication of laser degradation.
All eight probed ONUs on EPON0/7 are online with normal optical readings, so there is no ONU, splitter, or whole-port outage.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and the OID subtree, ruling out an OLT failure.
RADIUS authentication exists with no mismatches, sessions are normal at 2 in 24 hours with a 711-minute average duration, and the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1017 rather than VLAN 46.
No direct PON utilization or capacity counter was supplied, so shared congestion cannot be proven conclusively from the available data.

remediation.reason: Evening-only slowdown with stable optical levels, constant distance, healthy laser metrics, correct authentication and VLAN provisioning, and a responsive OLT is most consistent with shared PON congestion. The diagnosis is probable rather than conclusive because direct utilization counters were not provided, so capacity planning and verification are required instead of an automated remediation.
remediation.instructions: Collect peak-hour PON utilization, throughput, queue, and error counters for EPON0/7 and compare them with off-peak measurements. Identify affected subscribers and traffic patterns, then assess rebalancing, service-profile changes, additional capacity, or splitting the PON as appropriate. Monitor performance after the change.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The issue is time-dependent and the optical link and ONU population are stable; resetting the ONU is unlikely to resolve shared evening contention.
Optical power, variation, distance, and TX bias are within normal ranges, with no evidence of fibre or splitter degradation.
TX bias is healthy and stable, providing no indication of laser ageing.
The OLT and PON remain responsive, and there is no evidence of an OLT, PON port, or router failure.
The customer is correctly provisioned on VLAN 1017 rather than VLAN 46.

escalation.review_reason: Shared PON congestion is probable but not confirmed because peak-hour utilization, throughput, queue, and error counters were not provided; human verification and capacity planning are required.
escalation.summary: The customer reports evening slowdown, with observed speed declining to 1.19 kbps versus a 5.72 kbps seven-day mean. Optical levels, TX bias, distance, sessions, authentication, VLAN provisioning, ONU status, and OLT health are normal, with no evidence of fibre, ONU, PON-port, router, or OLT failure. The likely cause is shared evening PON congestion. Collect and compare peak- and off-peak EPON0/7 utilization and performance counters, then evaluate rebalancing, profile changes, added capacity, or PON splitting.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
